mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between monthly changes in real personal income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) and monthly changes in S&P 500 returns over the prior 12 months implies that further income growth will continue to support equity prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 growth and S&P 500 returns turns negative or the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive when GDPC1 growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages signals a labor market expansion with slack, which boosts consumer demand and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average during a period of otherwise stable GDP growth signals a housing sector downturn that negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average while GDPC1 is stable
regime_hint: stable GDP growth with housing weakness
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls below its 12-month moving average while GDPC1 is stable.
